questions.prompt: According to the passage, why could pedestrians feel hot above a relatively cool pavement?
options: The sensors measured only underground temperatures.
Pale pavements prevented all air movement.
Reflected sunlight could increase the heat reaching their bodies.
Tree shade increased the temperature of the pavement.
The study took place during the winter.
questions.explanation: Açık renkli yüzeylerin yansıttığı güneş ışığı yayaların aldığı ısıyı artırabilir.
questions.passage: A team studying heat in a coastal city placed sensors on streets with different types of pavement. Pale surfaces were generally cooler than dark ones at midday. Yet pedestrians did not always experience greater comfort above the cooler surfaces. Some pale pavements reflected more sunlight towards people, increasing the heat they received. Streets with tree shade tended to provide more consistent relief. The researchers stress that their observations cover only one summer and a limited range of street designs. They recommend evaluating surface temperature alongside the conditions people actually experience, rather than treating either measure as a complete description of urban heat.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by the passage?
options: Pale pavement should be removed from every city.

Surface temperature alone always indicates pedestrian comfort.
Assessing urban heat requires attention to more than the temperature of the ground.
questions.explanation: Yüzey sıcaklığı ile insanların deneyimlediği koşullar birlikte değerlendirilmelidir.

questions.prompt: Why did the programme introduce practical group activities?
options: To replace all fluent speakers with written teaching materials.
To help learners use the language in ordinary situations.
To restrict the language to the telling of traditional stories.
To stop participants from discussing contemporary topics.
To prove that every learner progressed at the same rate.
questions.explanation: Pratik grup etkinlikleri, kayıtların tek başına sağlayamadığı gündelik kullanım deneyimini kazandırmak için eklenmiştir.
questions.passage: A community language programme initially focused on recording older speakers telling traditional stories. Although the recordings preserved vocabulary and pronunciation, younger learners found it difficult to use the language in everyday conversations. The programme then added small group sessions in which fluent speakers and learners planned meals, repaired objects and discussed local events together. Participants began using a wider range of expressions outside class. The organisers still valued the recordings, but concluded that access to an archive should be accompanied by opportunities to use the language for practical purposes. They cautioned that progress varied among learners and that attendance alone did not guarantee confident speaking.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by the passage?
options: Preserving language materials can be usefully combined with meaningful opportunities to practise speaking.
Recorded stories prevent learners from acquiring everyday expressions.
Regular attendance ensures that all learners become confident speakers.
Language archives become worthless once group activities are introduced.
Practical activities are effective only when traditional vocabulary is excluded.
questions.explanation: Program hem kayıtları değerli bulmuş hem de bunların pratik konuşma fırsatlarıyla desteklenmesi gerektiği sonucuna varmıştır.
